title: fix(lint): judge an object's defaultRowScope in the RLS predicate and org-axis rules
body:
Fixes #24452

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`@objectstack/lint` now judges an object's default row scope (`ObjectSchema.defaultRowScope`) the way it judges a permission set's row policy.

- **`validateRlsPredicateEnforceability`** (`packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts`). The per-policy body of the walker is moved into one function, `judgePolicy(graph, policy, site, options)`. The walker calls it for each `permissions[].rowLevelSecurity[]` entry, as before, and for each `objects[].defaultRowScope`, with the declaring object as the target. There is no second lowering implementation: the default goes through the same `isSupportedRlsExpression` verdict, the same shape explanation (`rls-predicate-unenforceable` / `-unparseable` / `-over-budget`), the same reference pass (`-unknown-field`, `-unknown-user-variable`, the type and comparand faults, the list-holding and cross-class arms) and the same engine read-scope pass. Severity is `error` for both sources.
  - Finding path: `objects[N].defaultRowScope.using` / `.check`.
  - `where`: `default row scope "NAME" of object "OBJECT"`. No part of a default's finding mentions a permission set (pinned).
  - The permission-set leg is byte-for-byte unchanged: same `where`, `path`, message and hint (every existing pin passes unedited).
- **`validateOrgAxisRedLines` rule ①** (`validate-org-axis-red-lines.ts`) also judges a default whose `using` / `check` reads `parent_organization_id`, at `objects[N].defaultRowScope.CLAUSE`, with the same message and hint. The reason is the rule's own: once the security plugin applies the default, it is a Layer-1 policy like any other, so walking the org parent there builds the same second hierarchy. The file's `## Scope` table and its "object-level RLS" note now name the one object-level policy key that is declared.
- **`os explain`** (`rule-explanations.ts`). The shared `RLS_DROPPED_USING` paragraph (used by all five `rls-predicate-*` entries) now covers both sources. For a permission set's policy, the object disappears for every holder of the set that carries it. For an object's `defaultRowScope`, which is applied only when the caller's sets carry no row policy for the object and operation, the default is always the only applicable policy. So a dropped default makes the object disappear for every caller it applies to, and a caller whose set carries its own row policy for the object is not affected. The `rls-predicate-unenforceable` entry's first paragraph also says it judges both places a row policy is declared. No other entry of that file is touched.
- Changeset `.changeset/24452-default-row-scope-lint.md`, `@objectstack/lint` patch: a new authoring-time finding on a shape that was silent before.

## Why the severity is the same (measured on the reader, not assumed)

PR #24451 (the runtime half, merged as `94e60c00f` and merged into this branch) makes `collectRLSPolicies` hand the default to the same admission, the same `getApplicablePolicies` filter and the same `RLSCompiler` an authored policy reaches. A non-lowering `using` is dropped with the same WARN and fails closed to `RLS_DENY_FILTER`, and #24451 pins that on the same predicate in both forms. The one runtime difference is that a default is never OR-ed with a sibling, because it is applied only to an empty collection. That makes the "this policy vanishes from the OR" branch impossible for a default, and the explanation says so. It is no reason for a different severity: the lint's bar for `error` is that no reading of the metadata behaves as written, and that holds for a default whose predicate cannot lower.

**Ordering.** #24451 landed while this PR was in progress, and this branch has it merged, so the explanation's account of a dropped default is what `main` does now.

## Pins

New file `packages/lint/src/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.default-row-scope.test.ts`. Every object fixture passes `ObjectSchema.safeParse` first.

1. A default whose `using` does not lower is reported (`rls-predicate-unenforceable`, `error`, `objects[0].defaultRowScope.using`, the `where` above), and no part of the finding mentions a permission set.
2. A default `check` that does not lower is reported at `.check`, with the write consequence ("admits no write").
3. The name-keyed map shape of `objects` is read too.
4. CONTROL: a lowering default (`select` and `all`), and an object with no default, report nothing.
5. Parity, five predicates (outside the pushdown subset, not CEL, an undeclared column, an unresolved `current_user` key, a list-holding key under `==`). The same predicate as a permission-set policy and as a default earns the same rule, severity, message and hint. Only `path` differs.
6. Both sources in one stack are reported, permission sets first.
7. The engine judge is handed a `select` default's `using` with the declaring object (`lead`, `{ operation: 'find' }`), and its refusal is reported at the default. CONTROL: an `update` default is not handed to it.
8. `runAuthoringRules('validate', …)` (the CLI registry door) reports the default under `rls-predicate-unenforceable`.
9. `os explain` for `-unenforceable`, `-unknown-field` and `-unknown-user-variable` carries the both-source wording.

`validate-org-axis-red-lines.test.ts`:

- new cases: a default `using` that walks the org parent is flagged (array form; `where` and `path` asserted; no "permission set" in it), a default `check` is flagged (map form), and CONTROL: a membership-scoped default is silent;
- the structural meta-guards are extended, not loosened. The declared-key guard now expects `object` to read `defaultRowScope` / `name` / `systemFields` / `tenancy` (all on `ObjectSchema.shape`) and adds a `scope` receiver checked against `DefaultRowScopeSchema.shape`. The clause-list guard checks both clause loops against their schemas. The reachability guard expects four `findings.push` sites and has a spec-valid default-row-scope fixture reaching the new one.

**Pin sweep.** I searched the whole repo for `rls-predicate-unenforceable` / `RLS_PREDICATE_UNENFORCEABLE` and for the reworded sentence (`disappears for every holder of the permission set`, `vanishes from the OR`). The two lint pins on the old sentence (`validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.test.ts`, the unknown-field and unknown-user-variable cases) still match, because the new text keeps that clause for the permission-set source. The new both-source assertions are in pin 9 above. The consumer pins (`packages/cli/test/rls-policy-authoring-admission.test.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`) assert permission-set paths only, and they pass unedited. No object in the tree declares `defaultRowScope` outside tests (`git grep` over `examples/` and every non-test source), so no linted example changes verdict.

**Ablation.** Run once on `ed2d826c13`, the first commit, after it was committed and before any merge (the line it mutates is unchanged since), then reverted, through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` under a `trap` restore:

- the change: `const scope = obj.defaultRowScope;` became `const scope = undefined as unknown;`;
- the anchor went from 1 to 0, and the blob from `bbb07af6453f` to `7dbfe87353be`;
- the new pin file then gave **11 failed / 3 passed**. The 3 passing are exactly the controls (lowering default, non-read-scope default, explain wording);
- the restore put the blob back at `bbb07af6453f`, equal to `HEAD`, with `git diff HEAD` empty;
- the observed direction was red, as expected. The tests import the rule from source (`./validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.js`, no `exports` hop), so no `dist` rebuild was involved.

## Tests and gates

Every reading below is on the final head `0db86b5479`. That head carries `origin/main` `45bec43cd` merged in (with #24451 and #24474), and every run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`. Each exit code below is the command's own, captured before any pipe.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test`: **146 files, 6896 passed**, exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck`: exit 0. That run includes `check:test-typecheck`, so the new test file compiles under `tsconfig.test.json` with the debt ledger unchanged.
- Consumers whose verdicts this rule feeds, run against the rebuilt `@objectstack/lint` `dist` (the closure was rebuilt by turbo on this head):
  - `packages/cli/test/rls-policy-authoring-admission.test.ts`: 39 passed;
  - `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`: 145 passed.
  - No example or app in the tree declares `defaultRowScope`, so no linted example changes verdict.
- `@objectstack/spec`:
  - `test:repo`: 70 files, **1162 passed**, exit 0;
  - `src/data/object-default-row-scope.test.ts` and `src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`: 86 passed;
  - `check:generated`: the only stale artifact was `content/docs/references/**`, from the describe edit, regenerated with `--fix` (only that one) and committed in `0db86b5479`.
- Derived gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives **110** commands for this diff (10 paths, merge base `45bec43cd`). All 110 were run on this head and every one exited 0. `--ran` reconciles: **110 derived, 110 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**.
- The four roster gates the derivation marks as keeping their roster under one of this diff's directories also exit 0: `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing` and `check:filter-alias-parity`.
- Declared to CI, not run locally: the whole-repo `pnpm lint` and the workspace type-check lanes.

### Surface beyond the claim (and why)

The claim's file surface is `packages/lint` plus the changeset. Measurement put one more file in this PR's way. `ObjectSchema.defaultRowScope`'s describe (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, written by #24451) told authors: "Authoring checks do not judge this predicate, so keep it inside the lowerable subset". This PR makes that sentence false. The edit is two sentences. The describe now says `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` judge the predicate, and that saving the object through the server does not run that check. The TSDoc says the same. With it come the three reference pages `gen:docs` regenerates and a `@objectstack/spec` patch line in the changeset. No schema shape, export or authorable key moved.

## Acceptance notes

- **The runtime publish gate does not run these rules on an `object` write.** `validateRlsPredicateEnforceability` is registered `runtimeTypes: ['permission']` (`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`), and `validateOrgAxisRedLines` is `CLI_ONLY`. So a Studio, REST `/meta` or MCP `object` save with a non-lowering `defaultRowScope` is not refused at that door by this PR. The CLI commands (`os validate` / `build` / `lint`) do judge it. The rule's positional `objects[N]` path is what the gate's per-write locating keys on (`isLocatedOnAnotherEntry`), so a `permission` write is not blamed for an object's default. Widening `runtimeTypes` is outside this card's claim surface (`authoring-rules.ts`). It needs a measured reading of the door, and the documentation table in `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx` that says this rule "reads `permissions[]`" would change with it. Not measured here, so not filed. Carrier: none.
- **#24451's edit to `validate-org-axis-red-lines.test.ts`** (title and docblock) merged into this branch without conflict.
- **Serial note.** PR #24474 (#23566), which edits other entries of `rule-explanations.ts`, has landed (`4bd7215a1`), and this branch merges `main` after it. The merge was clean.
